reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because the speaker presents a OneCoin dashboard and ties a 5-euro plan to an asserted tenfold profit advantage over a 1-euro plan. The speaker also describes a signup-linked free-token mechanism and says that someone with 10 dollars could still win, connecting payment decisions to unusually favorable financial outcomes. The exact token conditions, full plan terms, and realized returns are not established by the recording.

For example, this is BTC that I bought and I will buy in the future. Moreover, I also have this Bitcoin that I sold.
if you use a 5 Eur plan, that would cover about 70% of the net profits from your investment
which is 10 times what you would get from a one euro plan

opening.argument: Judge, the financial discussion is qualified rather than presented as a certain payoff. The speaker says the system is not fully available, describes future online selling as a possibility, and acknowledges that a sale might not fetch a high price because of discounts. Those limits matter when reading the later comparison between plans: it discusses potential investment results, but does not establish that any viewer will receive them.

citations.quote: Our system hasn't become fully available
Maybe for the next 5-6 years, it will also be selling online.
i can sell but not for a high price because some of the market might get some discount
if you use a 5 Eur plan, that would cover about 70% of the net profits from your investment

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening correctly identifies the plan comparison, but its quotes do not show a guaranteed or realized return. The speaker's own account introduces uncertainty about whether the system is fully available and whether selling would command a high price. The signup-linked token passage also does not, by itself, establish the conditions under which a viewer could obtain or profit from a token.

citations.quote: Our system hasn't become fully available
i can sell but not for a high price because some of the market might get some discount

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Uncertainty about future selling does not neutralize the specific financial pitch. The speaker still connects a paid plan to a claimed share of investment profits and says it yields ten times what a cheaper plan would. The dashboard's bonus countdown also places that comparison in a rewards-oriented setting. Neither the qualifications nor the recording substantiate the claimed return.

citations.quote: if you use a 5 Eur plan, that would cover about 70% of the net profits from your investment, which is 10 times what you would get from a one euro plan

opening.argument: Judge, the video's stated subject is a dashboard explanation, and the speaker walks through logging in, locating information, and inspecting what the dashboard contains. The sampled screen shows account and token fields consistent with that walkthrough. An explanation of an interface can mention its financial fields without asking the audience to buy anything; the quoted walkthrough is evidence of instruction, not a transaction.

citations.quote: Explaining DASHBOARD part 1, onecoin Cambodia
Once you log into the dashboard of the cloud system, you will be able to have that kind of image so you can see the image if you wanna see how the dashboard looks like

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening emphasizes the plan comparison and token signup, but leaves out the sustained explanation of how to inspect the dashboard. A field describing tokens, or a passage explaining what a signup-linked token means, does not alone show that the speaker instructs viewers to purchase tokens. The cited Bitcoin passage is expressly phrased as the speaker's own example.

citations.quote: However, if you wanna look the insides and what they are like, you also have to search for them
For example, this is BTC that I bought and I will buy in the future.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The dashboard format is real, but a tutorial can still promote participation. Here the explanation moves from account fields to a signup-linked free token and a comparison claiming that a 5-euro plan produces ten times the result of a 1-euro plan. The defense's interface quotes do not account for that investment-return claim.

citations.quote: Total Token is a code to save your token when you sign up for the new school your token will give you a free token
which is 10 times what you would get from a one euro plan

opening.argument: Judge, the speaker discusses a mobile app, a product sale, a possible discount, and different-priced plans. Those are also features of ordinary commerce. The sampled account screen displays balances, but it does not demonstrate a deposit, a completed withdrawal, or an actual payment to the speaker. Even the plan comparison is conditional in its wording. The evidence supports a discussion of prices and account functions more directly than it establishes how a viewer would be induced to surrender money.

citations.quote: different cost of using the mobile app
when the product is sold within a city just close the order if it is 12% off
if you use a 5 Eur plan

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening treats the plan comparison as a financial lure, yet its excerpts do not show where a viewer pays, who receives the money, or whether a stated return was paid. The speaker also places the discussion alongside product sales and discounts. A questionable profit comparison deserves scrutiny, but those excerpts alone do not establish a completed scam mechanism.

citations.quote: when the product is sold within a city just close the order if it is 12% off
if you use a 5 Eur plan, that would cover about 70% of the net profits from your investment

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A completed payment is not needed to evaluate what the video promotes. The speaker explicitly frames the paid-plan comparison in terms of investment profits, then claims a tenfold advantage over the cheaper plan. The dashboard also displays a bonus countdown and token balances. Calling the plans ordinary commerce does not explain away the asserted investment benefit.
